title: Life and Fate
subtitle: Reforge scythe and plow into sword's edge. Let iron learn to leave its sheath. Let our enemy know the taste of hunger.

items.text: Life and Fate
Militia Base, Bereggrad
He does not feel pain as the living do, but it has left its mark all the same. He must have endured unimaginable torment.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: His bodily structure is too fractured to store his arcane energy. The leakage is worsening his condition.
Charon's body is held together in an unnatural way. Like a man crushed a thousand times, his fragments no longer fit together as they should.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: How could the Manus do such a thing?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Why? He's got nothing to do with any of this.
Merel stands with her back to Charon, her shoulders hunched and trembling.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I should've gone with you, Charon.
Charon now lies on a stretcher. Silent and contained, like a black wall behind them.
Merel finally saw Charon's arcane skill for the first time. Vast and hollow, like death itself.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: No ...

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Merel. Merel?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Marsha, *sniffle* I ...
She instinctively turns to her, but Marsha grips her shoulders firmly, holding her back in place.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Don't turn around. I think Charon wants to tell you something.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: What? What is it, Charon?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Merel ...

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: *sob* Charon, I'm sorry! It's all my fault!
With a single word, Merel's words come rushing like a river breaking its banks.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: You protected me, walked with me all this way, hid me, kept me safe, and ... and after all that, after everything you've done for me, I left you there all alone!

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: If only I weren't such a weakling, if only I were brave like the others, I could've taken you with me, saved you for once.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: But ... but ...

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: It's all my fault. I'm useless. I should never have left you behind. If it weren't for me, you could've ... you could've ...

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: *whimper*
The words choke in her throat before they can be spoken.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: No, Merel ...
Charon finds a chance to piece together his broken speech.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You promised to run away when danger came.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Why do you remain here? Go. Find a safe place.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: No. I can't. I can't run away anymore. I shouldn't.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I should never have run in the first place.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: If I'd just gone back to the squad, if I hadn't asked to go with you, if ...

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: *whimper*
Merel is too overwhelmed to speak.
A pair of hands gently wipes the tears from her face.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Hush now. How are you supposed to help me fix Charon up if you keep crying like this?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Don't forget what we need to do.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Charon will be fine. As long as we can restore the vessel of his consciousness, he'll recover.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I'm the only one who can look at him right now, and I need a reliable assistant. Only the two of us can help him. Do you understand?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Yes. *sniff* Right. I understand.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Then take a moment and wipe your tears.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: It won't be an easy task, but it'll soon be over.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Just follow my instructions and give me what I need when I ask for it. Can you do that, Merel?
A boy steps onto a fallen stone pillar, the wreckage of the warplane in the church behind him.
It's been shot down, yet it still seems to posture in defiance—a grim reminder of how fragile this city is.

items.speaker: Citizen Representative
items.text: We will not be victims!

items.speaker: Citizens
items.text: We will not be victims!
One by one, people gather around Fyodor Petrovich, quickly forming a tight circle.

items.speaker: Citizen Representative
items.text: Save Bereggrad! Hand over Igor!

items.speaker: Citizens
items.text: Hand over Igor!
More and more voices join the chanting.
The rest of the residents linger at a distance. Some whisper behind covered mouths. Others lift anxious eyes to the sky, searching for bombs that may yet fall.
The chanting crowd clambers over the street barricades, only to be halted by gun barrels before the fortifications of the city defense headquarters.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Stop! Don't go any further!

items.speaker: Citizen Representative
items.text: Stand aside, kid. I need to talk to your commander.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: You can tell me. I'll pass it on.
Sergey feels a shove from the side.

items.speaker: Militiaman
items.text: Hey, I know this man. Let me talk to him.
The Bereggrad militiaman climbs onto the fortifications, standing taller.

items.speaker: Militiaman
items.text: Fyodor, take your people and turn back! Or are you here just to cause trouble?

items.speaker: Citizen Representative
items.text: Still standing strong with the cavalry, are we, Dima? Don't you know how many have sided with us?

items.speaker: Militiaman
items.text: Them? Pah, just little sheep following any dog that barks at them!

items.speaker: Citizen Representative
items.text: You idiots! All we have to do is hand over that Igor, and Krutov will leave us be! The choice is obvious!

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: You're the idiot! They're bandits! You can't trust a word they say!

items.speaker: Citizen Representative
items.text: And this Igor? Who is he?

items.speaker: Citizen Representative
items.text: No one here has ever even heard of him. It's no skin off our back to hand him over. You cavalry said you wanted to protect the city. Now is your chance!

items.speaker: Citizen Representative
items.text: If Krutov has some personal issue with Igor, then I say they solve it themselves on the steppe!

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: You don't know what you're talking about. The drink's pickled your brain. Just look at your nose.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: You've got no say here anyway. So shut it and go home.
A cacophony of boos erupts from the crowd.

items.speaker: Militiaman
items.text: Or you can use your enthusiasm to fight off the bandits and get our market back.
The commander turns from the window.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Tell the first battalion's commander to evacuate the citizens trapped outside. Just a few sharp soldiers. Don't worsen the situation.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Be careful. No misfires. Fyodor won't dare start a real fight. He'd sooner roll in his wealth than die.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: Yes, Commander.
Sternova leaves at the order.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: You taught Krutov well, Igor.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: He has driven a wedge between us. Old-fashioned, but effective. He knows we need both the militia and the citizens to hold Bereggrad.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: One whispered deal, and half turn against us.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: He will do anything to bring me a humiliating death.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Why? I never warmed to him, true, but I had no inkling his hatred ran so deep.
Igor falls silent, as if fishing his thoughts from the depths of a dark pond.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Like me, there was no turning back for him after São Paulo. He can only continue down the path he has laid.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Since the deal with Manus Vindictae, he has resented me. He claims I shorted him for his sacrifice.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: He also believes our break from the Manus was a grave mistake. He wishes to wrest more power from them.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: But I never promised him power; I promised him a chance at survival. Still, he calls the "boon" a sacred thing that will grant him the power of a god.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Krutov took my choice as weakness. Now, he is obsessed with proving that his path is the right one.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: He wants to kill me, to take the "boon," to prove his worth to the Manus.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: We can take advantage of this.
Outside, arguments between the cavalrymen and citizens rise and fall along the street.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: One thing is certain: this decisive battle will not be inside the city. We cannot stay here long.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Let us leave together, Ivan. We will discuss our strategy on the way to camp.
